active.title: Five-a-Side Football at Aspria Arts–Loi
active.description: Show up to the open five-a-side sessions at Aspria near the European Quarter and you'll find a rotating cast of EU staffers, local students, and expats who all play harder than you expect.
active.bonus: Score a goal and celebrate it as if you've just won the World Cup — full performance, no apology.

active.title: Bike the Promenade Verte Circuit
active.description: The 60km Promenade Verte loops the entire Brussels Capital Region through forests, parks, and villages that feel nothing like the city center you left an hour ago.
active.bonus: Complete the full 60km loop without using any navigation app — paper map or nothing.

active.title: Early Morning Run Along the Canal to Laeken
active.description: Running Brussels' canal north from Sainte-Catherine to the Laeken greenhouses before the city wakes is the fastest way to understand the city's industrial-to-royal geography.
active.bonus: Stop at the Atomium on the return and do 10 burpees in front of it before anyone intervenes.

social.title: Aperitivo Hour at Le Comptoir des Galeries
social.description: The bar inside the Hotel des Galeries draws Brussels' creative and media crowd at golden hour — perfectly made Negronis, no tourists, sharp conversation.
social.bonus: Start a conversation with whoever is sitting alone at the bar and find out what they actually do for work.

social.title: Political Debate Night at Théâtre National
social.description: The Théâtre National regularly stages public forum nights and politically charged performances that remind you Brussels is an actual capital, not just a chocolate shop.
social.bonus: Introduce yourself to one stranger during the interval and ask them the most provocative political question you can think of.

social.title: Late Night at Delirium Café
social.description: Delirium holds a Guinness record for beer selection — 2,000+ labels — and its labyrinthine basement fills nightly with an international crowd that actually knows what they're ordering.
social.bonus: Let a stranger at the bar pick your next beer without telling them your budget.

chill.title: Comics Afternoon at Centre Belge de la Bande Dessinée
chill.description: The Belgian Comic Strip Center in a restored Horta building is one of the strangest, most specifically Belgian pleasures in a city full of them.
chill.bonus: Find a Tintin original panel on display and recreate the character's exact pose for a photo.

chill.title: Stroll and Sit in Parc du Cinquantenaire
chill.description: The Cinquantenaire's triumphal arch and manicured lawns are Brussels at its most imperial and unhurried — bring nothing and do absolutely nothing structured.
chill.bonus: Find a spot of grass with a direct sightline to the arch, lie flat on your back, and stay there for 20 minutes minimum.

chill.title: Read at Café Walvis, Molenbeek
chill.description: Walvis is a neighbourhood brown café in Molenbeek with mismatched chairs, Belgian draught, and exactly zero reasons to check your phone.
chill.bonus: Leave whatever book or magazine you brought on the table for the next person when you leave.

chill.title: Afternoon at Musée Magritte
chill.description: The world's largest Magritte collection sits in a neoclassical mansion on Place Royale — three floors of surrealism that you absorb at whatever pace your brain allows.
chill.bonus: Find the painting that unsettles you most and spend ten uninterrupted minutes sitting in front of it.

foodie.title: Dim Sum Crawl in Quartier Chinois
foodie.description: The blocks around Rue Sainte-Catherine hide a genuinely good Cantonese scene — dim sum carts, roast duck windows, and bubble tea joints that Brussels tourists almost never find.
foodie.bonus: Order one dish entirely by pointing at someone else's table without knowing what it is.

foodie.title: Sunday Market Brunch at Flagey
foodie.description: The Sunday organic market around Place Flagey in Ixelles pulls the best producers from across Belgium — graze on raw milk cheese, charcuterie, and sourdough while Ixelles slowly wakes up around you.
foodie.bonus: Spend exactly €15 and build the best possible picnic — no supermarket backup allowed.

foodie.title: Gueuze Tasting at Cantillon Brewery
foodie.description: Cantillon is a living lambic brewery in Anderlecht where you drink funky, spontaneously fermented gueuze straight from barrels in the actual production space.
foodie.bonus: Buy a bottle of Kriek and carry it openly through the Midi neighborhood on your way home.

foodie.title: Frites at Maison Antoine, Place Jourdan
foodie.description: Maison Antoine's double-fried frites with andalouse sauce from a paper cone on Place Jourdan is the single most honest meal Brussels will ever hand you.
foodie.bonus: Order three different sauces and rank them out loud to the person next to you in the queue.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Bozar Restaurant
foodie.description: Housed inside Horta's art nouveau masterpiece, Bozar serves technically precise Belgian cuisine that matches the architecture's quiet ambition course for course.
foodie.bonus: Ask the sommelier to pair a Belgian natural wine you've never heard of to your main and trust them completely.

adventure.title: Urban Bouldering at Arkose Brussels
adventure.description: Arkose in Molenbeek is the city's sharpest climbing gym — high-quality routes, a strong local scene, and a post-climb natural wine bar that makes the whole thing feel very Brussels.
adventure.bonus: Ask a stranger on the wall to show you the hardest route they can currently complete and attempt it.

adventure.title: Forest de Soignes Night Walk
adventure.description: The beech cathedral of Soignes after dark turns one of Europe's most underrated urban forests into something genuinely cinematic and slightly unnerving.
adventure.bonus: Stand completely still for 60 seconds in total darkness away from any path and just listen.

adventure.title: Canal Kayak from Tour & Taxis
adventure.description: Paddling the Brussels canal from the repurposed Tour & Taxis freight depot gives you a water-level view of industrial heritage that no tour bus can touch.
adventure.bonus: Wave at someone eating on a canal-side terrace and get them to wave back.

adventure.title: Rooftop Sprint at the Atomium
adventure.description: Belgium's most surreal landmark earns its reputation up close — the panoramic top sphere at 92 meters reframes the entire city in steel and sky.
adventure.bonus: Find the oldest date stamped on any information panel inside and photograph it.
